summary.short: Mexican statute (DOF 18 March 2025) governing the electricity sector: national grid planning and control, generation and supply permits, transmission and distribution, retail supply and the wholesale market run by CENACE. Federal jurisdiction. Contains no AI-specific provisions.
summary.long: Ley del Sector Electrico, published in the Diario Oficial de la Federacion on 18 March 2025. This record covers part 1 of 2: Articles 1 to 175 and the Chapter X heading; the remaining text is not in this document. The law regulates planning and control of the Sistema Electrico Nacional, and generation, including permits for plants of 0.7 MW or more, distributed generation, self-consumption, cogeneration, long-term production and mixed investment schemes. It sets rules for transmission and distribution, including interconnection, metering and suspension of service, and for commercialization, including basic supply and last-resort supply. It also covers qualified users, small systems, storage, electromobility, rights of way and land negotiations, local content, and a wholesale market operated by CENACE, with market rules, CNE monitoring and a universal energy service fund. Further provisions cover consultation with indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities, social impact assessments, clean energy certificates, tariff methodologies, standards and reliability measures. Administrative sanctions are referred to the law in Article 106, but penalty amounts are not set out in this part. Federal jurisdiction applies. No AI-specific provisions appear.

notes: Part 1 of 2: Arts. 1 to 175 (through Capítulo IX). Capítulo X (De la Información) and later provisions are in part 2. The text is the consolidated 'TEXTO VIGENTE' from the DOF of 18-03-2025, with page headers. Decree Articles Primero and Segundo are elided ('…….'), so companion laws in the same decree are not in this text. The Reglamento and administrative general provisions referred to throughout are not part of this text. Internal points: Art. 96 refers to 'la fracción I del artículo 90', but Art. 90 has no fractions; the written request is in Art. 91 I. Art. 97 names 'Secretaría de Energía' inline where elsewhere the text uses 'Secretaría'. Art. 12 VI (state must keep at least 54% of injected energy) and Art. 40 I (state entity holds at least 54% of a mixed-investment project) use the same figure for different subjects. Relations and entities with no registry ID or no LEI/ticker in the text use empty strings in place of null, per the schema's string type. Part 2 covers Arts. 176-188 and the transitional provisions of the law, plus the decree's transitional articles. The decree's reforming articles are shown only as 'ARTÍCULO CUARTO A ARTÍCULO DÉCIMO.- ………' in this text, so their content is not annotated. Art. 186 refers to 'Capítulo II del Título Octavo' for sanctions, while the sanctions chapter in this part is Capítulo II of Título Noveno; the text is recorded as written. Fraction and item labels in the extracted text are partly displaced by page layout, so fraction references (e.g., Art. 185) should be checked against the official PDF. The TESL repeal is partial, as stated in Transitorio Décimo Tercero.
